analysis.evidence: בֶּעָנָן, “in the cloud,” specifies where the bow will be. The next clause, וּרְאִיתִיהָ, “and I will see it,” refers to the bow present there.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ precedes a Qal perfect third-person feminine singular verb agreeing with הַקֶּשֶׁת, “the bow.” The weqatal form has future reference in the covenant promise.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67854:7, 67853:3.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ incorporates the definite article before עָנָן, a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: The feminine suffix refers to הַקֶּשֶׁת, the bow in the cloud. God says he will see the bow, and לִזְכֹּר gives the purpose of seeing it, to remember the everlasting covenant.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ precedes a Qal perfect in the first person common singular. The third-person feminine singular suffix הָ is the direct object. The verb continues the promise with future force.

analysis.evidence: God sees the bow in order to remember בְּרִית עוֹלָם, the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature. The bow signals that God will uphold that covenant.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לִ marks purpose before the Qal infinitive construct זְכֹּר. God, the speaker of וּרְאִיתִיהָ (“I will see it”), is also the subject of the infinitive.

analysis.evidence: בְּרִית עוֹלָם means “an everlasting covenant.” God sees the bow in the cloud and remembers this covenant, whose parties the verse identifies as God and every living creature on earth.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state before עוֹלָם, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh

analysis.evidence: In בְּרִית עוֹלָם, עוֹלָם describes how long the covenant endures. God sees the bow and remembers the covenant with every living creature on earth. The verse gives no endpoint for that covenant.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state. It completes the construct phrase בְּרִית עוֹלָם.
analysis.sense: duration with no stated endpoint (in context)

analysis.evidence: After בְּרִית עוֹלָם ‘an everlasting covenant’, בֵּין introduces אֱלֹהִים ‘God’ as one party. The following וּבֵין introduces כָּל נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה ‘every living creature’ as the other.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.
